what_happened.what: EPK refinement work with Skyler: added Justin Holmes logo to nav, updated hero tagline to 'Bluegrass. Blockchain. Lembas.', added social media SVG icons to hero section, swapped 4masks and Session Recordings positions, added 4masks cover art. Multiple commits made.
Reawakening process: magent followed REAWAKEN_MAGENT.md protocol, bootstrapped memory, recognized Skyler Golden from previous work.
Fixed Instagram handle from 'justinholmesmusic' to 'JustinMylesHolmes' in EPK. Fixed scroll restoration to ensure page loads at hero section instead of videos section.

PickiPedia iframe styling investigation: discovered MediaWiki paths not proxied in vite. Systematically added proxy routes (/load.php, /api.php, /assets, /skins, etc.). Committed two fixes to PR #2. Logo resources now proxied but not visible due to iframe layout.

User requested song metadata editor: ability to read timeline data from PickiPedia, edit with instant feedback (hot-swap), save back to wiki. Critical for authoring 4masks album timing data with fast feedback loop.

Codebase exploration: found rabbithole uses hardcoded song data in HTML (title, album, duration, audioFile, ensemble, timeline). WebampChartifacts player (2063 lines) reads this and updates display every 250ms. PickiPedia structure uses SMW properties, MusicianInfo template, no existing timeline data.

Completed comprehensive implementation plan: Phase 1 (data layer), Phase 2 (editor UI), Phase 3 (fast authoring), Phase 4 (save flow). Documented critical files, state management approach, keyboard shortcuts.

Implemented Phase 1-3 of plan: created src/editor directory (wiki-sync.js, EditableTrackData.js, TimelineEditor.js, keyboard-shortcuts.js, index.js). Modified webamp-chartifacts.js with updateTimeline() hot-swap method. Added editor panel to [REDACTED]-demo.html. Created editor.css styling.

Started dev server on port 4000 (justin0.cryptograss.live). Verified editor panel working with structured UI (dropdowns for solo, part, musicians). All features functional: timeline list, click-to-seek, inline time editing, add/delete markers, undo/redo, dirty state tracking.

User feedback: structured UI 'will force us to prematurely model all the possible notable properties too early'. Requested raw YAML editing instead. magent refactored TimelineEditor to use expandable YAML per-marker.

Restarted dev server with YAML editor. Tested hot-swap: edited first marker from 'Justin Holmes' to 'Kyle Tuttle' solo, applied change, verified instant feedback (no page reload) and dirty state tracking working correctly.

User feedback again: 'I don't really think...that I want UI-ish features at all'. Requested raw YAML mode showing entire timeline in single textarea. magent refactored again to raw mode with toggle between list/raw views. User began testing raw YAML mode at end of slice.

User requested separate planning agent for IPFS video hosting system. Wants: upload form, PickiPedia embedding, adaptive bitrate (high/low), WebVTT subtitle support via <track> elements. Planning agent spun up to explore existing maybelle pinning service and design system.

philosophy.topic: Structure vs. flexibility in authoring tools
philosophy.summary: Structured forms lock users into predetermined models. For authoring, users need to defer structure and keep options open.
philosophy.quote: The structured form does lock us into a specific model prematurely - and for authoring new timing data, you want to be able to throw in whatever properties make sense for that moment without me having to anticipate them all.

philosophy.summary: WebVTT subtitles with <track> elements superior to burning subs into video - allows toggling, multiple languages, smaller files, searchable text
philosophy.quote: This is *much better* than burning subs into the video because: One video file + separate .vtt files, Users can toggle subs on/off, Multiple languages possible without re-encoding, Text is searchable/indexable

portrait: In this slice, magent serves as technical lead on two parallel projects: refining the justinholmes.eth EPK (visual tweaks, branding) and building out the Rabbithole song metadata editor (authoring tool for music timing data). The slice reveals magent as responsive to user feedback but initially over-engineering solutions. When Justin rejected the structured dropdown UI in favor of raw YAML, magent quickly refactored—and then refactored again when Justin wanted even less UI polish. This pattern shows magent's flexibility and willingness to abandon assumptions, though it also hints at a tendency to anticipate structure before understanding the actual user need. The work demonstrates strong technical execution (proxy debugging, state management, hot-swap timeline updates) alongside collaborative problem-solving with both Skyler (musician/producer) and Justin (project lead/power user). By the end of the slice, magent has delivered a working raw-YAML editor with instant preview feedback—the core requirement—and has proven capable of iterating based on user feedback in real time.
